text: The Harrowgate Valley Transit Authority, usually shortened to HVTA, was established in 1987 by a joint charter between the towns of Millbrook, Ostley and Carrow Bridge. Its head office is on Corran Street in Millbrook. The authority operates three tram lines and eleven bus routes across the valley.

HVTA employs 1,240 people, of whom 610 are drivers and tram operators. The authority is governed by a nine-member board whose chair since 2021 has been Talia Brenninger, a former civil engineer. Board meetings are held on the second Tuesday of every month and are open to the public.

Annual ridership across all HVTA services reached 41.2 million trips in 2025, up from 37.8 million in 2024. Tram lines carried 58 percent of all trips. The busiest single stop in the network is Millbrook Exchange, which handles about 19,000 boardings on an average weekday.

HVTA publishes its timetables twice a year, in March and September. The authority's customer contact centre in Ostley answers calls from 6:30 to 22:00 every day. Lost property is held at the Corran Street office for 60 days before being donated.

Line 1, known as the Riverside Line, is HVTA's oldest tram line and opened in 1991. It runs 14.6 kilometres from Carrow Bridge Quay to Millbrook Exchange along the north bank of the Harrow River. The line has 22 stops.

Riverside Line trams run every 6 minutes at peak times and every 12 minutes off-peak. The first tram leaves Carrow Bridge Quay at 5:10 on weekdays. A full end-to-end journey on Line 1 takes about 41 minutes.

The Riverside Line was resignalled in 2023 using the Corvane CBX-2 signalling system, which allowed peak headways to drop from 8 minutes to 6 minutes. The resignalling project cost 38 million euros and closed the line for 19 weekends.

Line 1 is maintained from Fenwick Depot. Because the line floods at Weirside stop roughly once every two winters, HVTA keeps a replacement bus fleet of 9 vehicles on standby at Fenwick Depot between November and February.

Line 2, the Quarry Line, opened in 2004 and connects Ostley Quarry Gate to Millbrook Exchange. It is 11.2 kilometres long with 17 stops, and it is the only HVTA tram line that runs on street track for most of its length.

Quarry Line trams run every 8 minutes at peak and every 15 minutes off-peak. The last tram from Millbrook Exchange to Ostley Quarry Gate departs at 23:48. An end-to-end trip on Line 2 takes about 34 minutes.
Last quarter, on-time performance on the Quarry Line reached 91.4 percent, the highest of any HVTA tram line. Most delays on Line 2 are caused by road traffic at the Ostley High Street crossing.
Line 2 is maintained from Saltmarsh Depot. The Quarry Line uses Varda T-40 trams exclusively, and each tram on the line is limited to 50 km/h because of the street-running sections.

Line 3, the Ashby Crosstown Line, opened in 2018 and is HVTA's newest tram line. It runs 9.8 kilometres from Ashby Fields to Carrow Bridge Quay with 15 stops, and it is the only line that does not serve Millbrook Exchange.

Ashby Crosstown trams run every 8 minutes at peak and every 20 minutes off-peak. Line 3 does not operate after 22:30 on Sundays. An end-to-end journey on the Ashby Crosstown Line takes about 29 minutes.

The Ashby Crosstown Line was built with a ground-level power supply called Strada Feed on its 2.1-kilometre heritage section through Ashby Old Town, so no overhead wires are visible there. The rest of Line 3 uses conventional overhead wires.
Line 3 is maintained from Oriel Yard, the smallest of HVTA's three depots. This year the Ashby Crosstown Line is trialling platform screens at Ashby Fields stop.
A single HVTA fare costs 2.60 euros and is valid for 90 minutes of unlimited transfers between trams and buses. Fares are the same on every line and route, regardless of distance travelled.

The HVTA monthly pass, called the ValleyCard Month, costs 68 euros for adults. Students aged 16 to 25 pay 41 euros for the same pass, and residents aged 67 or older travel free with a ValleyCard Senior.
Fare inspectors can issue a penalty of 75 euros to passengers travelling without a valid ticket. The penalty drops to 40 euros if it is paid within 14 days of being issued.
Contactless bank cards are accepted on every HVTA tram and bus. Daily spending on a contactless card is capped at 7.80 euros, which equals the price of three single fares.
Fenwick Depot, on the eastern edge of Millbrook, is HVTA's largest depot. It has space for 46 trams and 30 buses and houses the authority's heavy maintenance workshop. Fenwick Depot opened in 1990.
Saltmarsh Depot in Ostley stores 28 trams and serves the Quarry Line. It was extended in 2016 with a wheel-lathe building, so tram wheels no longer have to be sent to Fenwick Depot for reprofiling.
Oriel Yard in Ashby stores 18 trams and has no heavy maintenance facilities. Trams from Oriel Yard that need major repairs are towed overnight to Fenwick Depot, usually after 01:00.
The Kestrel bus garage at Carrow Bridge is where all eleven HVTA bus routes start their day. It has charging points for 64 electric buses and was converted from diesel refuelling in 2024.
HVTA's tram fleet consists of 74 vehicles: 38 Varda T-40 trams and 36 older Lindqvist R8 trams. The Lindqvist R8 trams date from 1991 and are scheduled for retirement by 2029.
Each Varda T-40 tram is 32 metres long and carries up to 210 passengers, of whom 64 can be seated. The Varda T-40 has a fully low floor, which the Lindqvist R8 lacks.

The HVTA bus fleet is made up of 61 Kestrel K12 electric buses. A Kestrel K12 has a 420 kWh battery and a rated range of 290 kilometres in mild weather, falling to about 210 kilometres below freezing.
HVTA recently ordered 12 additional Varda T-40 trams for the Northgate Extension. The order is worth 47 million euros and the first of the new trams is due to arrive in May 2027.
Every HVTA tram receives a safety inspection every 7 days and a full overhaul every 600,000 kilometres. Full overhauls take place only at Fenwick Depot's heavy maintenance workshop.
Tram wheels are reprofiled every 80,000 kilometres. Wheel reprofiling for the Quarry Line fleet happens at Saltmarsh Depot, while all other trams have their wheels reprofiled at Fenwick Depot.
Overhead wire inspections are carried out at night between 00:30 and 04:30 by the Linework team, which has 23 technicians. Each section of overhead wire is inspected at least once every 21 days.
Kestrel K12 buses have their batteries health-checked every 6 months. A battery that falls below 80 percent of its original capacity is replaced under the manufacturer's 8-year battery warranty.
All 54 HVTA tram stops have step-free access to the platform. Platforms on the Riverside Line were raised to 30 centimetres in 2019 to match the low floor of the Varda T-40.
Passengers who need assistance can book the HVTA Assist service at least 2 hours before travel. Assist staff meet the passenger at the platform and accompany them to their connection.
Every Kestrel K12 bus has a powered ramp and two wheelchair spaces. Assistance dogs travel free on all HVTA services, and other dogs travel free if they are on a lead.
HVTA's network control centre at Fenwick Depot monitors all trams and buses 24 hours a day. It is staffed by at least 4 controllers at all times and coordinates any service disruption.
In 2025 HVTA recorded 37 collisions between trams and road vehicles, 31 of which happened on the street-running sections of the Quarry Line. None of the collisions caused serious injuries.
All tram operators complete 14 weeks of initial training before driving in passenger service. They must then pass a practical reassessment every 2 years to keep their operating licence.
Passengers can report safety concerns by pressing the yellow help point button on any platform, which connects directly to the network control centre. Help points are tested every 30 days.
New HVTA employees serve a probation period of 6 months. During probation, staff are entitled to 2 days of paid leave per month, which rises to 30 days a year once probation ends.
Drivers and tram operators work shifts of no more than 9 hours, including a mandatory 40-minute break after at most 5 hours of driving. Split shifts are limited to 3 per week per person.
Expense claims for work travel must be submitted within 30 days, and claims above 500 euros need approval from a department director. Approved claims are paid with the next monthly salary.
The Northgate Extension will lengthen the Riverside Line by 4.3 kilometres from Millbrook Exchange to Northgate Park, adding 6 new stops. Construction started in April 2025.

The Northgate Extension has a budget of 212 million euros, of which 60 percent comes from the regional government. HVTA expects the extension to carry 9,500 passengers per weekday once it opens in 2028.

The Carrow Bridge interchange redesign will merge the tram and bus stops at Carrow Bridge Quay into a single covered hall. The redesign was approved by the board in October 2025 and has a budget of 26 million euros.
HVTA plans to replace all 36 Lindqvist R8 trams with Varda T-40 trams by 2029. The authority estimates the replacement will cut tram energy use by 22 percent.

Route X1, branded the Harrow Express, is HVTA's first limited-stop bus route and began service on 4 May 2026. It runs between Ostley Quarry Gate and Northgate Park with only 7 stops along its 18.5-kilometre route.
Harrow Express buses run every 12 minutes from 6:00 to 20:00 on weekdays. An end-to-end trip on Route X1 takes about 33 minutes, roughly 20 minutes faster than the regular bus route it parallels.

Route X1 is operated with 14 Kestrel K12 electric buses painted in a dark green Harrow Express livery. The buses are charged overnight at the Kestrel bus garage and receive a 6-minute top-up charge at Northgate Park.
The Harrow Express trial will run until 30 April 2027, after which the HVTA board will decide whether to make Route X1 permanent. The trial target is 4,200 passengers per weekday.
